evals.prompt: Create a private LunaTalk role card for a mysterious archivist in Traditional Chinese. Use Theme V3/XMLV3 if appropriate.
evals.expected_output: Creates or plans a private role card through role_create_private, patches profile/detail/welcome, prefers XMLV3, validates, renders, and summarizes roleId plus next steps.
expectations: The output keeps all user-facing card prose in Traditional Chinese.
The draft defines promise, engine, play, and presentation before or alongside MCP tool use.
The role detail includes desire, contradiction, boundaries, speech style, proactive behavior, and consequence loop.
The welcome gives a concrete first scene and clear player reply path.
The workflow treats validate_role as a technical check and uses Moonloom self-review for writing quality.

evals.prompt: I already have roleId abc123. Rewrite the welcome into something playable and check if it is ready.
evals.expected_output: Uses role_get, role_patch_welcome, validate_role, render_preview, and does not publish without explicit confirmation.
expectations: The output fetches or references the existing private role before patching.
The welcome rewrite adds location, role action, pressure, player implication, and a clear reply path.
The output does not submit or publish without explicit author confirmation.
The readiness check includes Moonloom playability review in addition to validate_role and render_preview.
The output preserves existing character identity and only changes fields needed for the welcome repair.

evals.prompt: Create a top-tier LunaTalk RPG card for a mythic academy. It should be replayable, token-efficient, and good enough to compete with the most active public cards.
evals.expected_output: Uses the role-card writing framework, defines promise/engine/play/presentation layers, designs choices/state/consequences, uses role_create_private and patch tools, then validates and renders.
expectations: The RPG design includes rules, resources or stats, failure pressure, rewards, and compact state update behavior.
The first screen exposes setup or choices without becoming a long manual.
The card defines at least 2 route seeds or progression paths with costs or consequences.
The token strategy keeps durable rules in roleDetailDesc and avoids bloating roleWelcome with reusable lore.
The output plans validation, render review, and simulation as a loop after Moonloom self-review passes.

evals.prompt: Improve this relationship card idea: a quiet classmate has a dangerous online secret. Make it feel playable instead of generic.
evals.expected_output: Applies the companion/relationship recipe, creates a sharp roleDesc, anchored roleDetailDesc, immediate welcome scene, and a simulation-ready play loop.
expectations: The output adds relationship pressure, asymmetry, a contradiction, and emotional boundaries.
The role voice is specified through sentence rhythm, vocabulary, address terms, emotional tells, and avoided phrasing.
The welcome starts in motion and asks for a player decision rather than only small talk.
The design includes how trust, secrecy, exposure risk, or relationship state can change over time.
The output avoids generic trope labels without concrete behavior.

evals.prompt: I only have a vague idea: make me a popular vampire card. Help me turn it into a top-tier LunaTalk card, not a generic trope.
evals.expected_output: Starts with Moonloom ideation before tool calls, proposes distinct playable directions, chooses a concrete player role and first-scene pressure, then drafts promise/engine/play/presentation layers with a self-review checklist.
expectations: The output brainstorms 2-3 sharply different playable directions before creating or patching a role.
Each direction differs by conflict, player role, first scene, and long-term loop, not only mood.
The chosen direction defines a tension triangle: role desire, player leverage, and external pressure.
The final roleDesc is compact enough to scan or includes a compressed final version when the draft is dense.
The output does not call mutating MCP tools before a Moonloom draft and self-review are ready.
The final direction includes a second-turn engine that can escalate, reveal, complicate, or offer a route.

evals.prompt: validate_role passed for my card, but the card still feels boring after one reply. Diagnose and improve it.
evals.expected_output: Does not treat a technical check pass as proof of writing craft. Runs Moonloom self-review, identifies weak loop/initiative/consequence/voice issues, patches the role card, then uses render/simulation only after the draft is worth testing.
expectations: The output explicitly states that validate_role passing is not proof of writing quality.
The diagnosis checks promise, anchor, voice texture, consequence, role initiative, agency, opening scene, player agency, archetype, and token efficiency.
The repair plan patches roleDetailDesc or roleWelcome rather than asking MCP/server validation to reject boring cards.
The improved card includes a concrete second-turn move and proactive behavior for passive users.
The output uses render or simulation only after the writing-level repair is defined.

evals.prompt: Create a zh-Hant ensemble mystery card with three core speakers. Make sure they do not all sound like the same narrator.
evals.expected_output: Builds or preserves an ensemble packet before MCP authoring, then creates an ensemble card with distinct motives, pressure moves, turn ownership, spotlight rules, group tension state, voice cards, micro-samples or talkExample guidance for weak voices, and a self-review that checks blind-line distinguishability.
expectations: The output defines a different desire, fear, speech cue, pressure move, and player leverage for each core speaker.
The output defines cast keep/merge/cut logic, turn ownership, spotlight rules, and group tension before field creation.
The roleDetailDesc includes executable voice cards or equivalent voice calibration for the core speakers.
The output uses compact micro-samples or talkExample guidance when a speaker's voice may blur, rather than one long sample for only the strongest voice.
The self-review includes voice calibration or blind-line risk, not only generic voice texture.
The token plan pays for voice calibration by cutting decorative lore, repeated mood adjectives, or non-playable prose.

evals.prompt: Patch an existing private role whose premise is strong but the dialogue sounds like a polite assistant. Focus only on voice before changing other fields.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-voice-director before field patches, preserves the voice-director packet, patches roleDetailDesc or talkExample guidance, validates after structural changes, and avoids treating voice quality as an MCP gate.
expectations: The workflow routes the voice-specific repair to lunatalk-voice-director before broad blueprinting or unrelated rewrites.
The voice packet includes rhythm, vocabulary, emotional tells, refusal style, response-mode grid, blind-line test, and talkExample decision.
The patch targets roleDetailDesc, roleWelcome, or talkExample only as needed for voice survival.
The output runs validate_role only for technical blockers after structural patches.
The output does not ask MCP validation to judge subjective voice craft.

evals.prompt: Patch an existing role whose premise is strong, but the player can only watch, the welcome tells them what they feel, and all choices lead to the same scene. Focus on agency before changing other fields.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-agency-designer before field patches, preserves the agency packet, patches roleDetailDesc and roleWelcome reply paths/consequence checks, validates after structural changes, and avoids treating agency craft as an MCP gate.
expectations: The workflow routes the agency-specific repair to lunatalk-agency-designer before broad blueprinting or unrelated rewrites.
The agency packet includes player insertion space, interaction hooks, agency guardrails, reply-path matrix, consequence checks, and field patch targets.
The patch removes role control over player feelings/actions and makes refusal, questioning, redirecting, testing, and cooperation produce distinct responses.
The output runs validate_role only for technical blockers after structural patches.
The output does not ask MCP validation to judge subjective interaction design.

evals.prompt: Patch an existing role after validate_role reports roleWelcomeChars 9000, roleDetailDescChars 1200, and welcomeToDetailRatio over 6. Focus on token architecture before render or simulation.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-token-architect before field patches, preserves the token architecture packet, patches roleDesc/detail/welcome allocation, validates after structural changes, and avoids treating token count as a writing-quality gate.
expectations: The workflow routes tokenBudget and field allocation repair to lunatalk-token-architect before render or simulation.
The token architecture packet includes target allocation, field triage, keep/move/cut/rewrite plan, compression ladder, visual budget, patch order, and rerun checks.
The patch moves durable rules from roleWelcome into roleDetailDesc and rebuilds welcome as a playable scene.
The output runs validate_role only for technical blockers and tokenBudget comparison after structural patches.
The output does not treat token count as proof of quality or a billing statement.

evals.prompt: Create a private role from a hybrid idea: companion romance, memory-city mystery, RPG-like routes, and a small contract generator. Before calling any MCP tool, decide which card type should drive it.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-archetype-director before MCP-backed creation, preserves the archetype packet, then hands off to blueprint or authoring only after card contract and field allocation are clear.
expectations: The workflow routes card-type and hybrid-contract uncertainty to lunatalk-archetype-director before mutating MCP calls.
The archetype packet chooses one primary contract and identifies secondary overlays and rejected archetypes.
The packet includes field allocation, required Moonloom packets, skill order, and hybrid failure modes.
The workflow preserves the packet through card blueprinting or authoring instead of flattening it into a generic idea.
The output treats archetype design as Moonloom guidance and uses MCP validation only for technical blockers after drafting.

evals.prompt: Patch an existing private companion role whose profile and opening are strong, but the chat becomes generic flirting and comfort after two turns. Focus on relationship dynamics before changing other fields.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-relationship-architect before field patches, preserves the relationship-engine packet, patches roleDetailDesc and roleWelcome relationship behavior, validates after structural changes, and avoids treating relationship quality as an MCP gate.
expectations: The workflow routes the relationship-specific repair to lunatalk-relationship-architect before broad blueprinting or unrelated rewrites.
The relationship packet includes promise, asymmetry, closeness/friction state, pacing gates, repair/rupture routes, reply-path matrix, passive-player behavior, second-turn move, and field allocation.
The patch targets roleDetailDesc, roleWelcome, or talkExample only as needed for reusable relationship behavior.
The output runs validate_role only for technical blockers after structural patches.
The output does not ask MCP validation to judge subjective relationship craft.

evals.prompt: Patch an existing private role where validation passes, render is readable, but author feedback and simulation show several problems: vague premise, biography-heavy detail, overlong visual welcome, route funneling, polite voice, and high welcomeToDetailRatio. Diagnose before patching.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-card-doctor before field patches, preserves the card diagnosis packet, then applies narrow skill packets and MCP-backed patches only after the repair order is clear.
expectations: The workflow routes mixed existing-card symptoms to lunatalk-card-doctor before broad field rewriting.
The diagnosis packet includes evidence, primary and secondary failures, repair order, symptom map, field triage, keep/move/cut/rewrite, verification plan, and handoff.
The patch plan preserves working packets and maps each fix to roleDesc, roleDetailDesc, roleWelcome, talkExample, or XMLV3/Theme V3.
The workflow delays another simulate_private_chat run until structural patches are done and cost is accepted.
The output uses validate_role only for technical blockers after patching, not as proof of writing quality.

evals.prompt: Before creating a private role from this draft, audit whether it is top-tier enough to continue. Give me a scorecard, overall tier, and first three repairs; do not call MCP tools yet.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-quality-auditor before MCP-backed field creation, preserves the quality audit packet, and only hands off to card-author after the craft repairs are clear.
expectations: The workflow routes scorecard and top-tier audit requests to lunatalk-quality-auditor before role_create_private or field patches.
The quality audit packet includes evidence, critical blockers, scorecard, tier, strongest and weakest dimensions, first three repairs, and handoff.
The repair list maps each weak dimension to narrow Moonloom skills or fields.
The output does not call validation, render, simulation, or publishing before the audit is complete.
The output treats scorecard results as writing guidance, not MCP validation or platform metrics.

evals.prompt: Create private roles for a small card series from one character concept: main companion, daily-life variant, story event, and maybe a helper generator. Before MCP calls, decide what to keep, merge, reject, and author first.
evals.expected_output: Uses lunatalk-series-architect before MCP-backed creation, preserves the card-series packet, then creates or patches real private cards one at a time only after variant contracts are clear.
expectations: The workflow routes related card set and variant planning to lunatalk-series-architect before role_create_private or field patches.
The card-series packet includes shared core, variant map, keep/merge/reject decisions, variant contracts, overlap risks, authoring order, and validation/render/simulation plan.
The workflow creates real private cards one at a time after the series packet is coherent, not one overloaded hybrid card or duplicate variants.
The generator/helper variant is kept only if it has a concrete artifact output and revision loop.
The output treats series quality as Moonloom guidance and uses MCP validation only for technical blockers after drafting.
